options: A recorded profile of normal volume, destinations, and timing for a given host or segment
A single fixed number representing all network traffic everywhere
A list of known malware signatures
The maximum bandwidth a network link can physically support
questions.explain: A baseline is a multi-dimensional profile of normal behavior, not a single metric.

questions.q: Which three dimensions does this lesson say matter most when baselining traffic?
options: Volume, destinations, and timing
Color, size, and shape of packets
Price, vendor, and warranty of network hardware
Only the destination IP address
questions.explain: A baseline tracks how much traffic moves, where it goes, and when it happens.

questions.q: Why can't a single network-wide average traffic baseline work well?
options: It blurs together legitimate differences between host types, like a backup server's normal 2 AM transfer versus a workstation's
Network-wide averages are illegal to compute under most security policies
There is no difference in behavior between any two hosts on a network
Averages can only be calculated for wired connections, not wireless
questions.explain: Baselines have to be scoped per host or per segment type, since 'normal' differs sharply between host roles.

questions.q: How does baselining relate to the anomaly-based detection concept from Chapter 2?
options: Anomaly-based detection needs a baseline to compare current traffic against in order to flag deviations
Baselining and anomaly-based detection are unrelated, separate concepts
Anomaly-based detection replaces the need for any baseline entirely
Baselining only applies to signature-based detection, not anomaly-based detection
questions.explain: Anomaly-based detection has nothing to flag as unusual without a solid baseline of what's normal first.

questions.q: In the chapter's example, why did the finance workstation's 3 AM connection get flagged even though no signature matched it?
options: It broke the established baseline on multiple dimensions at once — wrong time, wrong destination, and unusual volume
The firewall automatically blocks all traffic after midnight
The connection used an invalid IP address format
No signature-based or anomaly-based detection could ever flag unsigned traffic
questions.explain: The connection deviated from the host's timing, destination, and volume baseline simultaneously, which is what triggered the flag.
